title: Unintended Location Data Sharing
description: Child's device shares live GPS coordinates without explicit consent or awareness of the implications of continuous location tracking.

title: Location Metadata Linkage
description: GPS coordinates in transit contain metadata that can be used to link the child to specific locations, times, and potentially identify behavioral patterns.

title: Location Data Storage and Processing
description: Mobile App Backend receives and stores live GPS coordinates, potentially retaining sensitive location data beyond necessary retention periods.

title: Location data disclosure to third parties
description: Location history stored in DS1 may be accessed by unauthorized parties or shared with third parties without user consent, violating the minimality principle for personal data storage.

title: Excessive location data collection
description: Mobile App Backend may collect and share more location data than strictly required for the intended purpose, violating the minimality principle for data collection.

title: Location data confidentiality breach
description: Location history stored in DS1 may be accessed by unauthorized parties due to inadequate access controls or security measures.

title: Location data linkability in transit
description: Location data in transit between P1 and DS1 may contain metadata that can be used to link or identify users, enabling profiling or tracking.

title: Location data minimization violation
description: Mobile App Backend may collect location data that exceeds what is strictly necessary for the intended purpose, failing to apply the minimality principle.

title: Sharing of sensitive location data
description: The Family Account Store shares zone definitions containing personal location information (home, school, friend's house) with the Geofencing Engine, creating a privacy risk through the sharing of location data.

title: Identification through location metadata in transit
description: Data in transit between the Family Account Store and Geofencing Engine may contain metadata that could be used to link or identify the parties involved, potentially revealing relationships or access patterns.

title: Processing of location data for geofencing
description: The Geofencing Engine processes the received zone definitions to implement geofencing functionality, which may involve storing or using location data in ways that create privacy risks.

title: Location data shared without consent
description: The geofencing engine shares location-based arrival/departure notifications to the parent entity without explicit consent or appropriate privacy safeguards, potentially exposing sensitive movement patterns.
assumptions: Assumes location data is collected and transmitted as part of the geofencing notification mechanism.

title: Flow metadata enables party linking
description: The data flow itself contains metadata about the parties involved (source and destination entities) that could be used to link or identify individuals, even if the payload is anonymized.
assumptions: Assumes the flow metadata includes information about the originating and receiving entities.

title: Parent entity may store location data inappropriately
description: The parent external entity may receive and store location-based notifications without appropriate retention policies or access controls, leading to potential unauthorized access or misuse of sensitive movement data.
assumptions: Assumes the parent entity has the capability to store the received notifications.

title: Unintended consequences of location sharing
description: Sharing location-based notifications may have unintended consequences such as profiling, discrimination, or surveillance of individuals based on their movement patterns.
assumptions: Assumes the parent entity or third parties could use the location data for purposes beyond the original notification intent.

title: Parent shares child's sensitive personal information
description: Parent shares child's name, DOB, and school information during account registration and profile creation, which could be accessed by unauthorized parties if not properly protected.
assumptions: Parent may not be fully aware of data protection implications

title: Parent may provide inaccurate or incomplete child profile data
description: Parent may provide incorrect or incomplete information about the child's profile, leading to inaccurate records that could affect the child's future.
assumptions: Parent may not verify information before submission

title: Data in transit may be intercepted
description: Personal data transmitted from parent to mobile app backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission.
assumptions: Data may not be encrypted during transmission

title: Data in transit may be modified
description: Data transmitted from parent to mobile app backend could be tampered with during transmission, potentially altering child's profile information.
assumptions: Data may not be integrity-protected during transmission

title: Mobile app backend may store child's personal information insecurely
description: Mobile app backend may store child's sensitive personal information (name, DOB, school) without adequate security measures, increasing risk of unauthorized access.
assumptions: Backend may not implement proper access controls and encryption

title: Mobile app backend may unintentionally disclose child's geofence zone information
description: Mobile app backend may inadvertently expose geofence zone definitions to unauthorized parties, potentially revealing child's location patterns and habits.
assumptions: Geofence data may not be properly protected or anonymized

title: Unintended Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Stored account, child profile, and geofence zone data may be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through data breaches, unauthorized access, or improper sharing mechanisms at the destination data store.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 has appropriate access controls and encryption in place

title: Data Integrity Compromise at Destination
description: Stored personal data (account, child profile, geofence zones) may be corrupted, altered, or tampered with during storage, potentially affecting data accuracy and user trust.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 has appropriate integrity controls and backup mechanisms

title: Data Linkage and Re-identification Risk
description: Stored child profile and geofence zone data may be linked with other datasets to re-identify individuals or infer sensitive information about family members beyond intended purposes.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 has appropriate data linkage controls

title: Data in Transit Disclosure Risk
description: Data flowing from P1 to DS2 may be intercepted or exposed during transmission, particularly if using unencrypted or insecure communication channels.
assumptions: Assumes appropriate encryption and secure transmission protocols are in place

title: Excessive Data Collection at Source
description: Mobile app backend may collect more personal data (account, child profile, geofence zones) than strictly necessary for the intended service, violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: Assumes data collection is justified by service requirements

title: Location History Data Exposure at Source
description: Location history data is being shared from the DataStore to the Mobile App Backend, potentially exposing sensitive location patterns of users without explicit consent or appropriate safeguards.
assumptions: Location history contains personal movement patterns that could reveal sensitive locations, habits, and routines.

title: Identification Risk from Location History
description: Location history data can be used to identify and profile individual users, potentially enabling re-identification or linking to other personal data.
assumptions: Location patterns are unique enough to identify individuals, especially when combined with other data sources.

title: Location Data in Transit
description: Location history data is transmitted in transit between DataStore and Mobile App Backend, potentially exposing location information to interception.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or may be intercepted by third parties.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Location History
description: The Mobile App Backend may disclose location history to unauthorized parties or in unintended contexts during processing or storage.
assumptions: Access controls and authorization mechanisms may not be properly implemented at the destination.

title: Data Integrity Risk at Destination
description: Location history data may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during processing at the Mobile App Backend.
assumptions: Data integrity controls may not be sufficient to prevent unauthorized modifications.

title: Excessive Information Sharing
description: Parent may share more location data than necessary (e.g., historical location history, precise GPS coordinates) when inviting secondary guardian, exceeding the minimum required for the purpose.
assumptions: Parent may not be fully aware of the extent of data being shared.

title: Data Interception in Transit
description: Location data transmitted from parent to mobile app backend could be intercepted by third parties during transmission, potentially exposing sensitive location information.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over potentially unencrypted or insecure channels.

title: Inadequate Data Storage Safeguards
description: Mobile app backend may store location data without adequate security measures, potentially allowing unauthorized access, leakage, or misuse of the secondary guardian's location information.
assumptions: Backend storage lacks proper encryption, access controls, or retention policies.

title: Unauthorized location data sharing
description: Mobile App Backend shares child's live location with Secondary Guardian without explicit, informed consent from the child or parent, potentially violating privacy expectations and consent requirements.
assumptions: Assumes consent mechanism exists but may not be properly implemented or understood by the child/parent.

title: Location-based identification of child
description: Sharing live location data enables identification and tracking of the child, potentially enabling profiling or surveillance beyond intended purposes.
assumptions: Assumes location data is identifiable and can be linked to the child.

title: Unintended use of location data by guardian
description: Secondary Guardian may use the child's location data for purposes beyond the intended sharing context, such as tracking, monitoring, or sharing with third parties without consent.
assumptions: Assumes Guardian has discretion over how to use received data.

title: Location metadata in transit
description: Data flow itself may contain metadata about the parties (child, guardian, device) that could be used to link or identify individuals even if content is encrypted.
assumptions: Assumes standard data flow characteristics with potential metadata exposure.

title: Linkage via metadata in analytics flow
description: The data flow contains metadata about the parties (user, app, partner) that can be used to link or identify users across different contexts, even if the analytics are aggregated.
assumptions: Assumes metadata is preserved in transit and can be analyzed by third parties.

title: Potential user identification in aggregated analytics
description: The source process may share aggregated analytics that could still be used to identify individual users through re-identification techniques or correlation with other data sources.
assumptions: Assumes aggregation is not perfect and some identifying information may be retained.

title: Unintended data use by advertising partner
description: The destination external entity may use the analytics data for purposes beyond what was intended, such as building user profiles or selling the data to third parties.
assumptions: Assumes the partner has access to the data and may not honor intended use restrictions.

title: Unintended consequences from data sharing
description: The data flow may have unintended consequences, such as enabling the partner to track user behavior across different apps or services.
assumptions: Assumes the partner has access to the data and may use it for purposes beyond the stated funding purpose.

title: Non-repudiation of SOS message
description: The child's SOS/check-in message may not be verifiably attributed to the child, as there is no cryptographic signature or authentication mechanism to prove the message originated from the child.
assumptions: Assumes no digital signature or authentication is used for the manual check-in/SOS message.

title: Data integrity during transmission
description: The location data in the SOS message could be altered or tampered with during transmission between the child and the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network that may be vulnerable to interception or modification.

title: Data confidentiality during transmission
description: The location data and SOS message could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing the child's location to third parties.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over a network that may be vulnerable to eavesdropping.

title: Data availability failure
description: The mobile app backend may fail to receive or process the SOS message due to system failures, network issues, or service outages, potentially delaying or preventing the parent from receiving critical location information.
assumptions: Assumes the mobile app backend is not always available and may experience failures.
